description: Marsh Migration and Thin-Layer Placement on Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USFWS, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. By prioritizing wetland restoration, managing predicted marsh migration, and eradicating nutria, the refuge has increased the resiliency of remaining refuge wetlands and helped maintain wildlife habitats and important ecosystem services. The integration of nature-based solutions, such as facilitating marsh migration, provides human well-being and biodiversity benefits. Coverage: Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge (2024). The toolkit gives Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge as the location, 2024 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
